entries.name: SAP SE investor relations (measured IR domain)
entries.reason: THE IR-SCAN SAMPLE: the brief's one proven IR-scan measurement (Andrew's Call 4, same brief@eb9cedded6 s.3) queried 'SAP SE investor relations' and resolved, via `display_link`, to 'www.sap.com > investors' -- HTTP 200, 18.4 KB, 10 organic results, 'all correctly SAP IR.' The one domain the scan has actually touched at this cut, distinguished from the `link` redirect-wrapper trap the same finding documents; source.py's own PASS_INPUT (lib/research/rules/source.py@5818c6ac3d) is this exact measured shape.

owner: UNASSIGNED -- Andrew names the owner (C-NO-CONTACT: not Adam's team directly)
seed_rule: PROPOSE a domain here iff it is named, by a LANDED battery finding, as one of exactly two things: (1) THE SA ROUTE -- a domain a live, Active estate Lambda already fetches from (measured: the seven seeking-alpha-* Lambdas, CRO brief AMGT_RESAPP_LAMBDAS_PEERS_IRSCAN_20260910.md@eb9cedded6 s.1); or (2) THE IR-SCAN SAMPLE -- a domain the brief's own proven IR-scan measurement resolved via `display_link` (same brief@eb9cedded6 s.3, Andrew's Call 4), never the unresolvable `link` redirect wrapper the same section traps on. An owner applying this rule to a NEW candidate domain checks: is there a landed finding naming it, by domain, as an Active fetch route or a measured display_link resolution? If yes, PROPOSE it citing that finding as `reason`; a `link` wrapper, an aggregator page, a `source` display name with no resolved domain, or nothing landed at all is NOT a citation and does not qualify. EXCLUDED ON PURPOSE: marketscreener.com -- source.py's own REFUSAL_INPUT (lib/research/rules/source.py) names it as the aggregator-posing-as-IR trap the SOURCE rule exists to catch, so it is never itself a seed candidate no matter how many times the scan touches it. PROPOSED is the ceiling this rule reaches; ADMITTED is the owner's act, never this rule's.
